story: What Alaska's November 3rd governor ballot decides about AI compute, and what it does not

claims.claim: Republican governor candidate Dave Bronson said "I'm a big believer in data centers" at a Commonwealth North candidate forum in Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: "I'm a big believer in data centers. I know that might be unpopular with some folks here," said Bronson at a candidate forum hosted by Commonwealth North in Anchorage on Thursday.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: The same text appears on alaskapublic.org (September 21st) and countryjournal2020.com (September 18th). The forum is dated only as "on Thursday". Because the Beacon original ran Friday, September 18th, that Thursday is probably September 17th, but no page states it. Do not print a date for this forum. Keep the second sentence if space allows, because it is Bronson's own hedge.

claims.claim: Bronson said the data center groups he is talking to would produce their own electricity because they consider Alaska's grid power unreliable.
claims.verbatim: And the groups that I'm talking to, they said we're not going to take your electricity because it's not reliable. … We will produce our own, and we will move, and we will build our own data centers.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: This is the condition attached to Bronson's support and should not be trimmed. The full quote continues "That's good for us. That's a very strong revenue source." The ellipsis is the Beacon's. needs_softening is true, because the claim about the groups is Bronson's account of private conversations. Use "Bronson said".

claims.claim: At a September 8th forum in Anchorage, Republican candidate Treg Taylor said of data centers "I think we need to embrace it."
claims.verbatim: At a Sept. 8 forum in Anchorage, Taylor — the state's former attorney general — offered a similar perspective. "I think we need to embrace it," he said of data centers.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: The story text says Sept. 8. The photo caption on the same story puts Taylor at a Sept. 9 forum (see C11), so the date is in conflict. The article text is the safer attribution for the quote. Taylor also said "We have all the makings of a great place for a data center to thrive and produce good-paying jobs for Alaskans."

claims.claim: Taylor said any data center in Alaska must bring its own energy, and that electricity costs are his biggest concern.
claims.verbatim: He added that electricity costs are his biggest concern. Any data center must "bring their own energy," he said
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: This is the conditional on Taylor's support, and any use of C03 must carry it. Only "bring their own energy" is in quotation marks on the page. The rest is the Beacon's paraphrase, so quote only those four words.

claims.claim: Taylor said a data center "doesn't have to drive up costs if you do it correctly" and can produce a net savings for Alaska ratepayers.
claims.verbatim: "It doesn't have to drive up costs if you do it correctly. It can produce a net savings to the ratepayers in Alaska," he said.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: needs_softening is true, because this is a candidate's projection and not a fact. Attribute it as Taylor's claim.

claims.claim: Democratic candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said he supports a moratorium on data center development in Alaska until the Legislature passes a comprehensive regulatory framework.
claims.verbatim: "I support a moratorium on data center development in Alaska until the Legislature can pass a comprehensive regulatory framework for that development in Alaska," he said during a Sept. 8 forum in Anchorage.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: The quote is complete. The Beacon calls it "a temporary pause". The same text is on alaskapublic.org and countryjournal2020.com.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said any limits on data center development would be decided by negotiations between himself and the Legislature.
claims.verbatim: Any limits on development would be decided by negotiations between himself and the Legislature, he said.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: This is the Beacon's paraphrase, not a direct quote. It matters structurally, because a governor alone doesn't impose a moratorium in this telling.

claims.claim: Republican candidate Bernadette Wilson said by text message "I will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers that take our resources and spoil our lands."
claims.verbatim: I will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers that take our resources and spoil our lands.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: This was given "by text message", not at a forum. The quote is scoped to HYPERSCALE data centers, so don't widen it to all data centers. It was preceded by an attack on Kreiss-Tomkins' AI-employee donations ("better known as Chat JKT"). The story's subhead on countryjournal2020.com groups Wilson with Kreiss-Tomkins as advising "caution".

claims.claim: The Alaska Beacon story identifies Dave Bronson, Treg Taylor and Bernadette Wilson as Republicans.
claims.verbatim: Republicans Dave Bronson, Treg Taylor and Bernadette Wilson and the Democratic Kreiss-Tomkins
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: The scouts reported that outlets disagree on Wilson's party. I did not reproduce that. All three fetched pages (alaskapublic.org, ktoo.org and countryjournal2020.com) carry this identical sentence calling Wilson a Republican. No other outlet was checked on Wilson's label. The Beacon links to a September 9th story about a "post-primary ballot shuffle", so if the deck uses any label beyond "Republican", verify it separately.

claims.claim: The Alaska Beacon story identifies Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins as the Democratic candidate.
claims.verbatim: Democratic governor candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said that if elected, he will seek to temporarily ban new computing data centers in Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: This matches all three republications.

claims.claim: A photo caption on the Beacon story places Taylor, Bronson and Kreiss-Tomkins at a September 9th forum held by the Last Frontier Republican Club at the Petroleum Club of Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: Former Attorney General Treg Taylor, at right, speaks at a Sept. 9. 2026, forum held by the Last Frontier Republican Club at the Petroleum Club of Anchorage.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (photo by Yereth Rosen), republished by Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: There is a date conflict. The body text attributes the Taylor and Kreiss-Tomkins quotes to "a Sept. 8 forum in Anchorage", while this caption describes a Sept. 9 forum. These may be two different events. The body text's "Sept. 8 forum" links to a Beacon story dated 2026/09/09. The deck should say the quotes came from "a September 8th forum" per the article text and should not name the venue for those quotes. The same caption is on countryjournal2020.com.

claims.claim: The Alaska Beacon first published James Brooks's story on the governor candidates and data centers on September 18th.
claims.verbatim: SEPTEMBER 18, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Copper River Country Journal, reprinting the Alaska Beacon
claims.notes: alaskabeacon.com returns 403, so the original date comes only from the Country Journal's byline line "FROM THE ALASKA BEACON. BY JAMES BROOKS" followed by the date. Alaska Public Media's version is stamped "Published September 21, 2026 at 9:26 AM AKDT" and KTOO's is September 22nd. It is safest to cite "reported by the Alaska Beacon" with no date, or "September 18th, per a reprint".

claims.claim: The Beacon reports that the Alaska Senate voted 14 to 5 this year to pass a data center bill.
claims.verbatim: This year, the Alaska Senate voted 14-5 to pass a data center bill, but the House failed to take it up before the end of the legislative session.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: The Beacon does not name the bill number. SB 250 is identified by its sponsor Tobin (C15) and by BillTrack50 (C20 to C22). The primary vote record (akleg.gov BASIS and the Senate Journal) returned 403 and LegiScan returned 403, so the 14-5 tally and the vote date are single-sourced to the Beacon. Attribute it to the Beacon.

claims.claim: The Alaska House failed to take up the Senate-passed data center bill before the end of the legislative session.
claims.value: House failed to take it up
claims.verbatim: but the House failed to take it up before the end of the legislative session.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: This is corroborated by BillTrack50 (C21, C22). The last action was a House Community and Regional Affairs hearing on May 18th, and the bill was marked Dead on May 20th.

claims.claim: The data center bill's sponsor, Sen. Loki Tobin, D-Anchorage, will return to the Legislature next year.
claims.verbatim: The sponsor of the bill, Sen. Löki Tobin, D-Anchorage, will return to the Legislature next year
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: The page spells the name Löki. The sponsor is corroborated by BillTrack50 ("Löki Tobin (D)").

claims.claim: The Beacon reports that the next governor will likely be confronted with legislation similar to the Senate-passed data center bill.
claims.verbatim: the coalition majority that passed the bill is also likely to return, meaning that the next governor will likely be confronted with similar legislation.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: needs_softening is true, because this is a projection. Use "likely" and "according to the Alaska Beacon". SB 250 itself is dead (C22), so any 2027 bill would be a NEW bill. Don't write that "SB 250 comes back".

claims.claim: The Senate-passed bill would have regulated how data centers use electricity from public utilities and required them to create decommissioning plans.
claims.verbatim: That bill would have regulated how data centers can use electricity from public utilities and would have required them to create decommissioning plans.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: This is the Beacon's summary. The bill text on akleg.gov returned 403. The finer provisions (RCA approval of contracts, costs recovered from the data center, community benefit agreements, filing with DEC) appear only in BillTrack50's machine-generated summary and are killed. See the killed list.

claims.claim: The Beacon reports that one $500 million data center proposal on the North Slope intends to burn local natural gas for power and use Arctic air for cooling.
claims.verbatim: One $500 million proposal on the North Slope intends to burn local natural gas for power and use the natural cold air of the Arctic.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: The Beacon does NOT name STAK Energy. Equating this proposal with STAK's ADL 422741 lease (C23 to C27) is unverified. Keep the two separate on the slides, or say "a $500 million North Slope proposal" without naming it.

claims.claim: Gov. Mike Dunleavy is term-limited and can't run again this year.
claims.verbatim: Dunleavy is term-limited and cannot run again this year. Four candidates remain in the race to replace him.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: The page says "cannot". House style for the claim text is "can't". The same passage says Dunleavy "has backed data centers".

claims.claim: BillTrack50 lists Alaska SB 250 as "An Act relating to data centers; and relating to utility service for data centers," sponsored by Sen. Loki Tobin.
claims.verbatim: An Act relating to data centers; and relating to utility service for data centers.
claims.source_outlet: BillTrack50
claims.notes: This is BACKGROUND and out of window. It reproduces the official title. The primary source, the akleg.gov BASIS SB 250 page, returned 403, as did the bill PDF and the Senate Journal. Introduced 02/18/2026.

claims.claim: SB 250's last legislative action was a House Community and Regional Affairs hearing on May 18th.
claims.verbatim: House Community & Regional Affairs Hearing (08:00:00 5/18/2026 Barnes 124)
claims.source_outlet: BillTrack50
claims.notes: This is BACKGROUND. BillTrack50's status line also shows "Crossed Over 05/16/2026", which is consistent with Senate passage before May 16th. The Senate vote date itself was not found.

claims.claim: BillTrack50 lists SB 250 as dead as of May 20th.
claims.source_outlet: BillTrack50
claims.notes: This is BACKGROUND and consistent with C14. It is a tracker's status label, not an official one. Use "the bill died when the session ended".

claims.claim: The Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas issued a preliminary decision to offer STAK Energy Corporation a 50-year lease on the North Slope.
claims.verbatim: the Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Division of Oil and Gas (Division), has made a Preliminary Decision to offer a 50-year lease to STAK Energy Corporation
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: This is BACKGROUND and PRIMARY, under ADL 422741 and AS 38.05.070. It was published 5/12/2026 and last modified 5/18/2026. The notice itself is a PRELIMINARY decision. Whether a Final Finding and Decision has since been issued could not be confirmed from this page. See the killed list.

claims.claim: The proposed STAK Energy lease covers a 715.4-acre parcel.
claims.verbatim: for a 715.4-acre parcel located within Sections 1-4, 9-12, and 13-16, Range 13E, Township 6N, Umiat Meridian
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY.

claims.claim: The STAK Energy site is adjacent to the Dalton Highway about 26 miles south of Deadhorse.
claims.verbatim: adjacent to the Dalton Highway approximately 26 miles south of Deadhorse
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY.

claims.claim: The STAK Energy lease is for a natural gas-powered energy facility that includes modular high-performance computing units.
claims.verbatim: construction, operation, and maintenance of a commercial natural gas-powered energy facility, including modular high-performance computing units, on-site natural gas power generation infrastructure
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY. The notice says "high-performance computing", not "AI data center". Use the notice's own words.

claims.claim: The STAK Energy preliminary notice set June 15th as its original deadline for public comments.
claims.verbatim: All comments must be received in writing at the mailing address or email below no later than 4:30 PM Alaska Daylight Time on June 15, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: PRIMARY. The ORIGINAL deadline on the preliminary notice. The docket record cites a separate DNR notice, id 224224, extending comment to July 17th; that notice refused automated fetches on September 25th. Print no STAK comment date.

claims.claim: Alaska DNR proposes to convey approximately 19,950 acres of state land to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority.
claims.verbatim: proposes to convey approximately 19,950 acres (subject parcel) of State-owned land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY, under ADL 234762. It is a noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance and a Preliminary Decision. It was published 7/10/2026 and last modified 8/19/2026 2:39:33 PM. The notice does not mention data centers. The attachment is titled "Houston Industrial Park .810 Decision_PD.pdf". The data center link comes only from the Beacon (C32).

claims.claim: The proposed AIDEA parcel is about two miles north of Houston in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough.
claims.verbatim: approximately two miles north of Houston in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, within Township 18 North, and Township 19 North, all Seward Meridian.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY.

claims.claim: The AIDEA Houston conveyance notice set August 19th as its original public comment deadline.
claims.verbatim: The deadline for public comment is 5:00 PM, Wednesday, August 19, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY. Only timely commenters may appeal the Final Finding and Decision. The operative deadline became September 14th under a separate extension notice (id 224879), which is why this claim says original.

claims.claim: DNR says the AIDEA preliminary decision will be issued as the Final Finding and Decision without further notice if no significant change is required.
claims.verbatim: If no significant change is required, the Preliminary Decision and related actions including any minor changes and a summary of comments and responses, will be issued as the Final Finding and Decision
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: PRIMARY. This matters for the deck. A final decision can issue with no new public notice, so "final decision pending" can't be confirmed from this page. Write that no final decision appears on the notice as of the September 25th fetch, not that none exists.

claims.claim: The Beacon reports that AIDEA announced plans for a development that could include data centers in Southcentral Alaska.
claims.verbatim: particularly since the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority announced plans for a development that could include data centers in Southcentral Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: The Beacon does not name Houston or ADL 234762. Tying this to the Houston conveyance (C28) is an inference, so needs_softening is true.

claims.claim: The Air Force solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 seeks AI data center development at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station.
claims.verbatim: RFLP Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Center Development at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base, and Clear Space Force Station
claims.source_outlet: SAM.gov (U.S. General Services Administration)
claims.notes: PRIMARY and BACKGROUND. The office is FA8903 772 ESS PK. HigherGov mirrors the same title and says it was posted April 10, 2026. The SAM.gov search returned exactly one result, of type Solicitation, with isActive false and last modified 2026-07-15. No award notice was returned.

claims.claim: Responses to the Air Force AI data center solicitation were due June 29th.
claims.source_outlet: SAM.gov (U.S. General Services Administration)
claims.notes: PRIMARY. The page gives this as the responseDate field. It is corroborated by HigherGov ("June 29, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT"), and 21:00 UTC equals 5 p.m. EDT. The scouts' claim that the deadline moved from May 29th was not verified this pass.

claims.claim: The Air Force has offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land in Alaska to private companies for data centers.
claims.verbatim: It's offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land to private companies, though no projects have been awarded yet.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC (Shelby Herbert), via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Corroborated by KTUU/Your Alaska Link on September 16th ("The Department of the Air Force says 4,700 acres of military land in Alaska are underutilized."). The RFLP appendices giving acreage per base were not located.

claims.claim: No Air Force data center lease projects in Alaska had been awarded as of September 15th.
claims.verbatim: though no projects have been awarded yet.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC (Shelby Herbert), via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Corroborated by KTUU on September 16th ("So far, nothing has been approved.") and by the SAM.gov search, which returned no award notice (C33).

claims.claim: KUAC reports the Pentagon wants to build up to a dozen military data centers near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: The Pentagon wants to build up to a dozen new military data centers near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC (Shelby Herbert), via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: needs_softening is true. The figure is not in the SAM.gov record I fetched, and the solicitation describes commercial leases rather than "military data centers". Write "according to KUAC" and "up to a dozen".

claims.claim: Sen. Lisa Murkowski said she is not a proponent of data centers at JBER or Alaska's Interior installations because of an insecure energy base at this time.
claims.verbatim: "I am not a proponent of data centers down at JBER or at our Interior installations because we are not able to support them because of an insecure energy base at this time," she said.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC (Shelby Herbert), via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: The quote is complete. Keep "at this time", because it is conditional. The page does not say where or when she said it.

claims.claim: KUAC reports that the Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly is calling for a data center moratorium but can't tell the Pentagon what to do on military land.
claims.verbatim: Even though the Borough Assembly is calling for a data center moratorium, it can't tell the Pentagon what to do on military land.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC (Shelby Herbert), via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: This is the reporter's framing, not a legal source. It is the only sourced statement of the limits on local authority over federal land. Attribute it to KUAC.

claims.claim: Fairbanks North Star Borough Mayor Grier Hopkins said it is a different question whether local concerns about data centers trickle up to the Pentagon.
claims.verbatim: "I know that the bases at our level listen to what the impacts of the community would be," he said. "Whether that trickles up to the Pentagon is going to be a different question.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC (Shelby Herbert), via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Hopkins continues "But here locally, the relationship is strong enough that we are listened to." Keep that balance if the quote is used.

claims.claim: DeepGreen Cook Inlet has proposed a 100-megawatt subsea data center in Cook Inlet.
claims.verbatim: Federal documents describe the development as a 100-megawatt project, with most of its electricity intended for the underwater data center.
claims.source_outlet: Peninsula Clarion (Jeffrey Kennett)
claims.notes: Corroborated by ADN on September 24th ("a 100-megawatt subsea data center with as many as 350 underwater turbines and 66 'hives'"). The Clarion story is dated one day before the window, so label it background. The FERC eLibrary was not read.

claims.claim: The Center for Biological Diversity, the Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance and the Kenai Peninsula Borough have filed motions to intervene in the DeepGreen FERC proceeding.
claims.verbatim: So far, motions to intervene have been filed by the Center for Biological Diversity, Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance and the Kenai Peninsula Borough.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Bella Biondini)
claims.notes: In window. The count holds as of ADN's publication and may have grown since.

claims.claim: Comments, motions to intervene and competing applications on the DeepGreen project can be filed with FERC through November 2nd.
claims.verbatim: Public comments, motions to intervene and competing preliminary permit applications can be submitted through Nov. 2 under FERC project number P-15423-000.
claims.source_outlet: Peninsula Clarion (Jeffrey Kennett)
claims.notes: Corroborated by ADN on September 24th ("through Nov. 2"). The Clarion says the deadline moved from October 31st because that date falls on a Saturday, which checks out for 2026. November 2nd is the day before Election Day (C46), a juxtaposition the deck may state but should not dramatize.

claims.claim: Alaska Energy Authority CEO Curtis Thayer said AEA will file to intervene in and oppose the DeepGreen proposal.
claims.verbatim: "We're going to file to intervene and oppose it, just so we have a position," AEA CEO and Executive Director Curtis W. Thayer said. "We've had no communication with them."
claims.source_outlet: Peninsula Clarion (Jeffrey Kennett)
claims.notes: This is a stated intent, not a filing. ADN's September 24th list of intervenors (C42) does not include AEA, so do not say AEA has intervened. Keep "just so we have a position" to preserve the conditional framing.

claims.claim: Under Article III Section 25 of the Alaska Constitution, the head of each principal department is appointed by the governor, subject to confirmation by the Legislature, and serves at the governor's pleasure.
claims.verbatim: He shall be appointed by the governor, subject to confirmation by a majority of the members of the legislature in joint session, and shall serve at the pleasure of the governor
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Lieutenant Governor of Alaska
claims.notes: PRIMARY and BACKGROUND. The page is undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date. A first extraction pass mislabeled sections on this long page. A second, targeted pass returned Section 25 "Department Heads" in full. The constitution does not name departments, and no page fetched in this run states that Natural Resources is a principal department (akleg statutes returned 403). Say "state department heads", not "the DNR commissioner", unless another source is found.

claims.claim: Alaska's general election day is Tuesday, November 3rd.
claims.verbatim: Election Day Tuesday, November 3
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Division of Elections
claims.notes: PRIMARY. The page is undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date. November 3rd, 2026 is a Tuesday. The Beacon story itself gives no election date, only "before Alaskans vote this fall".

claims.claim: The Alaska Constitution lets the governor veto bills passed by the Legislature.
claims.verbatim: The governor may veto bills passed by the legislature. He may, by veto, strike or reduce items in appropriation bills.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Lieutenant Governor of Alaska
claims.notes: PRIMARY. This is Article II, Section 15.

claims.claim: A vetoed bill that is not a revenue or appropriation bill becomes law only with the votes of two-thirds of the Legislature's membership.
claims.verbatim: other vetoed bills become law by affirmative vote of two-thirds of the membership of the legislature
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Lieutenant Governor of Alaska
claims.notes: PRIMARY. This is Article II, Section 16. The extraction returned this clause as a fragment rather than the whole section, so confidence is a notch lower. Revenue and appropriation bills need three-fourths. SB 250's Senate margin of 14 to 5 is 14 of 20 senators, which exceeds two-thirds of the Senate alone, but an override counts the membership of the legislature (the context indicates both houses together). Do not compute override math on the slide.

claims.claim: A bill becomes law without the governor's signature if the governor neither signs nor vetoes it within fifteen days, Sundays excepted, while the Legislature is in session.
claims.verbatim: A bill becomes law if, while the legislature is in session, the governor neither signs nor vetoes it within fifteen days, Sundays excepted, after its delivery to him.
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Lieutenant Governor of Alaska
claims.notes: PRIMARY. This is Article II, Section 17. The adjournment rule, a longer period, was not captured.

claims.claim: Sen. Dan Sullivan said AI companies, not communities, need to pay the costs of producing AI.
claims.value: pay the costs of producing AI
claims.verbatim: AI companies, not our communities, need to pay the costs of producing AI.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Wil Courtney)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP material. The page is stamped "Sep. 16, 2026 at 6:36 PM AKDT" and the URL says 09/17. Sullivan also called for "clear safeguards around the highest-risk AI technologies".

claims.claim: Sen. Lisa Murkowski said she would welcome a serious effort to establish clear guardrails for the AI industry.
claims.verbatim: welcome a serious effort to establish clear guardrails for the industry that balance the benefits this technology can provide with the need to protect Americans.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Wil Courtney)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. This is a partial quote embedded in the reporter's sentence. Keep the "balance the benefits" clause.

claims.claim: The Beacon reports that Kreiss-Tomkins' campaign has received large donations from people employed by the AI company Anthropic.
claims.verbatim: While Kreiss-Tomkins' campaign has received large donations from people employed by the AI company Anthropic, those employees have tended to recommend restrictions on AI development as well.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by KTOO
claims.notes: needs_softening is true. The characterization of the donors' views is the Beacon's, so attribute it. No dollar figure is stated beyond "hundreds of thousands of dollars" in the lede. Wilson's quote (C08) uses this as an attack line, so present both neutrally or omit both.

claims.claim: DNR's preliminary decision on the STAK Energy lease says the authority to execute the Final Finding and Decision was delegated to the Division of Oil and Gas from the Commissioner of DNR.
claims.value: delegated from the Commissioner of DNR
claims.verbatim: The authority to execute this PD, the Final Finding and Decision (FFD), the Entry Authorization (EA), and the final perfected lease agreement was delegated to the Division of Oil and Gas from the Commissioner of DNR.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas, ADL 422741 Preliminary Decision
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY. Read by the showrunner on September 25th with scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py (16 pages, text layer present); full text kept at out/2026-09-25/primary/stak_pd.txt. Verbatim is whitespace-normalised.

claims.claim: The STAK Energy pad would host a natural gas-fired power plant designed to produce 1 to 3 gigawatts of electricity.
claims.verbatim: a natural gas-fired power generation system designed to produce 1-3 gigawatts (GW) of electrical power
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas, ADL 422741 Preliminary Decision
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY. Read by the showrunner on September 25th with scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py (16 pages, text layer present); full text kept at out/2026-09-25/primary/stak_pd.txt. Verbatim is whitespace-normalised.

claims.claim: DNR's preliminary decision describes the STAK Energy power and computing systems as behind the meter and not interconnected to the Railbelt or any other Alaska utility grid.
claims.verbatim: The power generation and computing systems are designed as a fully integrated, behind-the-meter configuration in which all generated electricity is consumed on-site by the HPC facility, which is not interconnected to the Railbelt or any other Alaska utility grid.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas, ADL 422741 Preliminary Decision
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, PRIMARY. Read by the showrunner on September 25th with scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py (16 pages, text layer present); full text kept at out/2026-09-25/primary/stak_pd.txt. Verbatim is whitespace-normalised.

claims.claim: The STAK Energy site sits about one mile west of the Dalton Highway at Milepost 390, west of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System.
claims.verbatim: The project site is located approximately one mile west of the Dalton Highway at Milepost 390, west of both the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation (AGDC) right-of-way and the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System (TAPS).
